_comment: How the App Store app on an iPhone shows the store assets: measured on screenshots of a live product
page, not specified by Apple. The iPhone is what the apps are made for (none targets the Mac), so
where a placement has a measurement here, its key art is judged against what the iPhone shows
instead of Apple's art safe area (app_store_creatives.json), which is the part every device keeps,
the Mac included, and leaves the iPhone header two thirds empty. A placement without one stays on
the safe area until someone measures it.
`header.aspect`: the iPhone shows the middle of the header at this aspect, in full height.
`header.measured`: that window in the screenshot's pixels; `overlays` are boxes in the same pixels
(left, top, right, bottom) of what the App Store lays over it, where no type or wish may sit. The
status bar runs the full width down to 150 px (50 pt): between its time and battery sits the notch
or the Dynamic Island (to 48 pt), which a screenshot does not show.
`header.points`: the window's width in points (the screenshot is @3x). With `measured` it turns a
canvas pixel into points on the phone.
`screenshots.frame_points`: the width in points of one portrait frame in the product page gallery,
`min_points`: the smallest type Apple's Human Interface Guidelines allow (11 pt); type in key art
that arrives smaller on the phone is a finding.
_source: iPhone screenshots 1170 x 2532 (@3x, 390 x 844 pt) of a live App Store product page, iOS 26, measured 2026-11-25:
header 1170 x 780 px from the top of the screen (exactly 3:2); gallery frame 681 x 1473 px at x 60.
